title: Derived module tensor computed on a K-flat first complex
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, with a chosen derived category of A-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any unbounded module complexes P and L, if P is categorically K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], then Q(P) tensor-derived Q(L) is isomorphic to Q(Tot(P tensor L)). There is no flatness or boundedness condition on L.

source.place: Derived tensor computation on K-flat models; ordinary-module specialization, proved in source FlatModel.

proof.text: Pass P to the homotopy category. The quotient K-flat equivalence makes its image K-flat. The derived tensor counit is then invertible on that first factor and arbitrary second factor. Compose the quotientCompQhIso on both inputs with this counit, the monoidal comparison of the homotopy quotient applied to P and L, and quotientCompQhIso on their total tensor. Their composite is the required isomorphism; this is precisely the existing source definition QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft. Every isomorphism is constructed from the counit and monoidal quotient comparisons, with no witness of mere existence used as data.
